reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports that Si+C additions form SiC in a FeCrNiCu HEA, yielding submicron particles and significant strength/hardness gains, but it does not address nanoscale dispersion, fracture toughness, or the effect on a caloric phase transition, leaving key premises unsupported.
premises: Adding Si and C to a high-entropy alloy can in-situ form SiC particles
In-situ SiC particles can be nanoscale and uniformly dispersed
SiC particles improve mechanical integrity (strength, toughness) of a high-entropy alloy matrix
A small volume fraction of SiC particles does not significantly disrupt the matrix phase transition responsible for the caloric effect
